title: First contacts: Russian from conversation to ideas
review_notice: AI-authored editorial draft with source notes. The AI teacher provides explanations, practice, feedback, and generated reference speech. No human review or native-speaker recording is claimed. Human recordings and expert feedback are optional additions; your friend does not need to prepare lessons or recordings.

units.title: Join a conversation
units.description: Speak from the first meeting: greeting, repair, script, and self-introduction.

units.title: Describe a shared world
units.description: Locate, request, possess, and distinguish things with meaningful endings.

units.title: Actions and relations
units.description: Use actor/patient, time, movement, and plans without making word-order guesses.

units.title: Read ideas early
units.description: Original supported scenes and first mathematical and philosophical language.

lessons.title: A first exchange
lessons.goal: Greet the AI teacher, acknowledge an answer, and close a short exchange.

explanations.title: An exchange, not a password
explanations.text: Привет is a useful informal greeting for a friend. Здравствуйте fits polite singular or plural address. The practice dialogue models a polite first meeting; the AI teacher can also rehearse an informal version with ты. With your friend, use the relationship you already have. Russian can omit a present-tense equivalent of English “am/is/are”: Хорошо can be a complete conversational reply.

explanations.title: Stress is part of the word
explanations.text: The acute accent is a learning scaffold, absent from most ordinary text. Start with the stress in приве́т and хорошо́. A strong syllable is not simply a syllable shouted more loudly; compare the AI teacher’s whole word and rhythm.

dialogue.title: A first exchange
dialogue.situation: A polite first meeting. The informal greeting Привет is an alternative to discuss, outside this modeled exchange.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Greet the AI teacher, ask how things are, respond, and say goodbye without reading a script.
lessons.sound_note: Listen to the final stressed syllables in приве́т and хорошо́. First imitate the whole phrase; isolate a syllable only if useful.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If it fits at breakfast, greet your friend with Привет! and perhaps ask Как дела? Let it be an ordinary moment; English is always available.

lessons.title: Keep the conversation going
lessons.goal: Ask for repetition, a slower rendition, and the meaning of a word.

explanations.title: Repair is a conversational skill
explanations.text: Повторите asks for another rendition; помедленнее asks for a slower one. Say Я не понимаю when the problem is understanding, then make a specific request. The -те form in повторите works for polite singular or plural address. Learn this useful request before learning a complete imperative paradigm.

explanations.title: One unknown word at a time
explanations.text: Point to or repeat the unfamiliar word before asking Что это значит? Keep the situation visible. Asking for help counts as successful communication; it is still assistance during an independent retrieval probe.

dialogue.title: Keep the conversation going
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: During the next lesson, use one repair phrase spontaneously when needed.
lessons.sound_note: Compare the rhythm of повтори́те and пожа́луйста with the AI teacher. Written syllables alone do not specify natural connected speech.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If you miss something during a meal, try a short request for repetition or meaning, then let the conversation continue.

lessons.title: Cyrillic through things
lessons.goal: Read a few real words and ask what an object is.

explanations.title: A small alphabet in use
explanations.text: In карта, к and т do not inherit the sounds of visually similar Latin letters. Read к-а-р-т-а with the AI teacher, then return to the whole word. Use the alphabet panel as a reference, not as a requirement to memorize all letter names before speaking.

explanations.title: Identifying and denying
explanations.text: Это книга identifies an object. Это не карта denies that it is a map; не normally stands before what is being negated. Russian has no articles equivalent to “a” and “the”; context supplies whether the object is new or familiar.

explanations.title: Letter and sound references
explanations.text: The alphabet cues describe common standard patterns and retain exceptions. In что, standard [што] is a word-specific starting point, not a replacement rule for ч. Listen to the AI speech model alongside these cues; the written cue alone is not the sound.

explanations.title: A small sound laboratory
explanations.text: Лук (onion in this picture task; also bow in other contexts) and люк (hatch) contrast a hard and soft л. The soft consonant is not a separate full “y” syllable. За́мок (castle) and замо́к (lock) share ordinary spelling but differ in stress and meaning. First compare the AI teacher’s audio models with pictures; then hide the spelling for a listening task. Hearing the contrast, writing its mark, and producing it remain separate goals.

dialogue.title: Cyrillic through things
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Point to a new picture, ask its name, and write Это … using the AI teacher’s supplied word.
lessons.sound_note: In ordinary standard pronunciation, что sounds like [што]. Do not infer a general rule that every written ч is pronounced ш.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If an object on the table catches your attention, ask its Russian name and use the new word once. There is no need to turn the meal into a quiz.

lessons.title: Say a little about yourself
lessons.goal: Introduce yourself and describe a language-learning goal.

explanations.title: Your name is yours
explanations.text: Меня зовут … is a useful introduction: literally something like “they call me …”. Substitute the name and pronunciation you actually use. The proposed spelling Эмбер and its stress are placeholders to confirm together, not an imposed Russian identity.

explanations.title: Speaking and studying
explanations.text: Я учу русский язык says that you are studying the language. Я говорю по-русски concerns speaking it. Я люблю фантастику can cover science fiction and fantasy; научная фантастика is more specifically science fiction. Do not force a favorite work or author before choosing one.

dialogue.title: Say a little about yourself
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Introduce yourself to an imagined new conversation partner and mention one real interest.
lessons.sound_note: Немно́го has stress on the first о. Compare the whole word with the AI teacher; do not pronounce each vowel as if it were stressed.
lessons.conversation_invitation: When interests come up, try one short sentence about what you like. Your friend already knows you; a formal introduction is not needed.

lessons.title: Where is it?
lessons.goal: Locate a person or object in a familiar room.

explanations.title: Where rather than where to
explanations.text: На столе and в комнате describe locations. Compare стол → на столе, комната → в комнате as concrete phrases. These are prepositional-case uses with на and в. This small pattern is not a full rule for all nouns or all uses of these prepositions.

explanations.title: A pronoun needs a referent
explanations.text: Он can refer to a man or to a grammatically masculine noun such as робот. A pronoun does not tell you that a robot is a person. Keep the referent visible while practicing, then ask where a new object is.

dialogue.title: Where is it?
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Ask where a real object is and report its location to another listener.
lessons.sound_note: Listen to столе́ versus ко́мнате: similar written endings need not be stressed. Compare the whole words before practicing endings.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If you are actually looking for a book or another object, try asking where it is. Follow the real answer, with English available.

lessons.title: Ask for something useful
lessons.goal: Request water or a book and notice the object form.

explanations.title: A role changes an ending
explanations.text: Вода names water; воду is the object in Я хочу воду. Книга becomes книгу in Дайте книгу. For these singular nouns on -а, the accusative has -у. Many other noun patterns differ; do not append -у to every object.

explanations.title: Directness and situation
explanations.text: Я хочу … states a want. In a café, Воду, пожалуйста is an ordinary short request in context. Дайте, пожалуйста is another useful request. With the AI teacher, compare how voice and situation affect how direct a request feels.

dialogue.title: Ask for something useful
dialogue.situation: A short café exchange: the server asks, the customer requests water, the server supplies it, and the customer thanks them.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Make a real request in Russian during the session, then acknowledge the response.
lessons.sound_note: Вода́ has final stress; во́ду has initial stress. The ending change and stress change both belong to the form. Compare the generated models of both forms and ask the AI teacher about the difference.
lessons.conversation_invitation: When you want water at a meal, try Воду, пожалуйста and then Спасибо. A useful little request is enough.

lessons.title: Have and have not
lessons.goal: Say what is available and what is missing.

explanations.title: A possession frame
explanations.text: У меня есть книга literally locates a book “with me”; learn it as a way to say “I have a book”. У вас asks about the person addressed; у робота names another possessor. This first encounter is about availability, not every use or omission of есть.

explanations.title: Absence changes the form
explanations.text: Compare есть карта with нет карты, есть вода with нет воды. Нет uses a genitive form here. Do not reuse the object form воду after нет. The meanings “not having” and “wanting” therefore give different cues for the ending.

dialogue.title: Have and have not
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Say one thing you have and one thing you do not have nearby; the AI teacher asks one follow-up question.
lessons.sound_note: Compare воды́ after нет with во́ду after хочу. Do not let a spelling drill stand in for hearing the different stress.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If an item comes up naturally, mention something you have or do not have nearby. No guessing game or preparation is needed.

lessons.title: Describe and choose
lessons.goal: Use adjective agreement to distinguish an object.

explanations.title: Agreement describes a noun
explanations.text: Новый робот, новая книга, новое слово show masculine, feminine, and neuter singular agreement in naming forms. Grammatical gender organizes noun patterns; it is not a claim about an object’s identity. Other cases require other adjective endings.

explanations.title: A useful contrast
explanations.text: Keep two objects visible so новый and старый help your listener choose. Какая agrees with книга in this question. Learn какой робот? and какое слово? later as related forms rather than treating какая as an invariant word for “which”.

dialogue.title: Describe and choose
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Describe a new object supplied by the AI teacher. Ask for its noun and gender if needed, then choose the adjective form.
lessons.sound_note: Listen to но́вый, но́вая, но́вое as whole words. Agreement is audible as well as visible; start with a short contrast.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If you are discussing a book or another object, try adding one description, such as new or old. Keep the focus on what you want to say.

lessons.title: Who sees whom?
lessons.goal: Read actor and patient from case across two word orders.

explanations.title: The first noun is not always the actor
explanations.text: Аня видит Веру and Веру видит Аня both say that Anya sees Vera. Веру is the accusative form. In the second sentence the listener already has Vera in mind and asks who sees her. Word order helps organize information; changing it is not always conversationally neutral.

explanations.title: Change roles, then change names
explanations.text: Вера видит Аню reverses who sees whom. Look for the endings before answering. Ask the AI teacher for a new pair of names of the same pattern, then interpret a sentence you have not memorized.

dialogue.title: Who sees whom?
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Interpret two unseen sentences with new names, then describe who sees whom yourself.
lessons.sound_note: А́ня and А́ню differ in the final vowel while initial stress remains. Ask for whole-word comparison; a correctly read ending does not establish listening discrimination.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If a story comes up, try saying who notices whom in one scene. Continue in English whenever that makes the conversation more interesting.

lessons.title: Now and yesterday
lessons.goal: Say when a reading action happens and notice process versus completion.

explanations.title: Past forms and your own speech
explanations.text: Читал and читала are masculine and feminine past forms; plural читали is another form. Choose self-description with the AI teacher according to your actual preference and context. The pack supplies alternatives rather than assigning Ember a past-tense gender.

explanations.title: Aspect is not just when
explanations.text: Читать / прочитать contrast an activity with a bounded result in these examples. Я читал книгу does not assert that the whole book was finished; Я прочитал всю книгу does. Imperfective can describe more than ongoing activity, and perfective more than “once”. These examples open a longer topic, not a complete definition.

dialogue.title: Now and yesterday
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Say what you are doing now and give one true statement about yesterday, using a supplied verb if needed.
lessons.sound_note: Listen to чита́ю, чита́л, прочита́л. The prefix adds a syllable; preserve the stress of the whole form rather than stressing every new piece.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If yesterday comes up over dinner, try one short true sentence about it. Use the past form you chose with the AI teacher.

lessons.title: Where, and where to?
lessons.goal: Distinguish location from a destination in a short exchange.

explanations.title: A destination is not a current location
explanations.text: Где? asks where someone is; куда? asks a destination. В школе locates Anya; в школу is the destination in the motion sentence. The movement can occur within a place too: a moving verb alone does not force every location phrase into the accusative.

explanations.title: A first motion distinction
explanations.text: Иду / идёт are useful for a current directed trip on foot. Russian distinguishes many kinds of movement; a vehicle trip and repeated trips need other forms in ordinary use. Дома means at home, домой means homeward; these are useful adverbs, not noun case endings to generalize.

dialogue.title: Where, and where to?
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Describe where you are now and one place you are going; ask the AI teacher for the appropriate motion verb.
lessons.sound_note: In идёт, keep ё visible. It is not interchangeable with е for learning this word. Compare the final stress in иду́ with идёт.
lessons.conversation_invitation: When you leave or discuss plans, try a phrase about where you are going. Use the wording that fits the actual trip.

lessons.title: Make a small plan
lessons.goal: Ask about ability and propose a shared reading activity.

explanations.title: A modal frame
explanations.text: Могу + infinitive expresses ability or possibility: могу прочитать. The infinitive does not take a person ending. Compare могу and можете while keeping the action constant. Context determines whether “can you” is a real ability question or a request.

explanations.title: Future and invitation
explanations.text: Буду читать is an imperfective future, without by itself asserting completion. Давайте читать вместе proposes a shared activity; it is useful with polite or plural address. With a ты relationship, давай is the corresponding informal singular form.

dialogue.title: Make a small plan
dialogue.situation: An original short exchange for the AI teacher and learner; the AI teacher can take either role and supply an unfamiliar word.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Propose a real small next step in Russian; negotiate the wording with the AI teacher.
lessons.sound_note: Могу́ and мо́жете have different stressed vowels and consonant shapes. Do not derive one pronunciation just by replacing the written ending.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If you genuinely want to read something together, try an invitation. The AI teacher can prepare a short informal version beforehand.

lessons.title: Original scene: a quiet station
lessons.goal: Read a tiny science-fiction scene and distinguish an observation from an inference.

explanations.title: Two kinds of knowledge
explanations.text: Слышит сигнал reports hearing a signal. Это человек? asks for an interpretation; Я не знаю withholds it. The short scene does not establish who sent the signal. Keep “what the text says” separate from a plausible story you add.

explanations.title: A supported reading bridge
explanations.text: Станция = station; тихо = quiet; слышит = hears; сигнал = signal; ответ = answer. На станции extends a familiar location frame, and ответа нет extends absence. Inspect a gloss when needed, then reread the original before explaining the scene in your own words.

dialogue.title: Original scene: a quiet station
dialogue.situation: An original supported scene or workshop exchange; all text is generated draft, not a published literary excerpt.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Add two original lines: one observation and one question. The AI teacher helps with vocabulary; preserve your intended meaning.
lessons.sound_note: Си́гнал would place stress incorrectly here: use сигна́л. First hear the AI teacher’s model; a correct accent mark is only a written observation.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If science fiction comes up, offer one line about the imagined signal and see where the story goes. No roles, performance, or review is required.

lessons.title: First mathematical sentences
lessons.goal: Read a conditional and distinguish some from every in a tiny mathematical setting.

explanations.title: Read the structure before every ending
explanations.text: Если … то … means if … then …. In this definition-like example, divisibility by two characterizes an even integer. A general implication alone does not license its converse; ask what each particular statement commits you to. Read the symbols n and n + 1 as symbols first; spoken mathematical notation needs a separately reviewed model.

explanations.title: Quantifiers and a definition
explanations.text: Существует means there exists; для каждого means for every. One example establishes this existence claim but cannot establish an arbitrary universal claim. Natural numbers may start at zero or one by convention; both statements here hold under either convention. Пусть introduces an assumption or chosen object in this mathematical use.

explanations.title: Specialist vocabulary
explanations.text: Чётное = even; делится на два = is divisible by two; больше = greater than; пример = example; доказательство = proof. This is an early supported bridge, not a claim that every inflection has already been taught.

explanations.title: Read scope in an unknown scene
explanations.text: The robot examples reuse the same quantifier distinction in a fictional situation, so knowing an arithmetic fact cannot substitute for reading. In Существует робот, который слышит сигнал, который introduces a description of that robot: “that hears a signal”. Не каждый робот hears the signal denies universality without saying that no robot hears it. A gloss is support, not independent comprehension.

dialogue.title: First mathematical sentences
dialogue.situation: An original supported scene or workshop exchange; all text is generated draft, not a published literary excerpt.

lessons.transfer_prompt: With the AI teacher, write one true существует claim and one true не каждое claim using this vocabulary.
lessons.sound_note: Чётное contains ё, which remains in ordinary and supported spelling here. Long phrases can be read in two chunks; do not imply that an unrecorded notation string has a reference pronunciation.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If mathematics naturally enters the conversation, try one small idea in Russian and finish in English if you prefer. Shared interest is the point.

lessons.title: First philosophical exchange
lessons.goal: State a belief, give a reason, and ask what would support it.

explanations.title: Belief, reason, and evidence
explanations.text: Я думаю, что … frames a belief. Почему? requests a reason; потому что introduces one. A response to questions can be offered as evidence without settling every philosophical question about understanding. The scene is an invitation to discuss, not an endorsed theory of minds.

explanations.title: A definition question is real conversation
explanations.text: Что значит «понимать»? reuses an everyday repair question to ask a conceptual question. Explain in English if the Russian is not yet available, then build one short Russian sentence with the AI teacher. Conceptual depth need not wait for effortless verb endings.

dialogue.title: First philosophical exchange
dialogue.situation: An original supported scene or workshop exchange; all text is generated draft, not a published literary excerpt.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Choose a real claim you are uncertain about. Say Я думаю …, give a reason with help, and name what remains unknown.
lessons.sound_note: Listen to понима́ет, понима́ть, поня́ть as words. Their related meanings do not make their sound sequences interchangeable.
lessons.conversation_invitation: During a real discussion, try one short Я думаю … statement or ask Почему? Let your friend respond to the idea rather than assess a lesson.

lessons.title: Reader, narrator, character
lessons.goal: Read a tiny original narrative and keep speakers and facts distinct.

explanations.title: The text has more than one voice
explanations.text: The narrator reports Anya opening a book and a cup on a table. The robot says nobody lives here. A character’s statement is not automatically the narrator’s assertion or the author’s belief. The cup invites an inference but does not prove current occupancy.

explanations.title: A negative pattern in context
explanations.text: Никто не живёт is an ordinary Russian negative pattern: никто and не work together rather than canceling each other into a positive. Кто-то means someone. Learn these as a useful contrast first; a full account of Russian negation comes later.

dialogue.title: Reader, narrator, character
dialogue.situation: An original supported scene or workshop exchange; all text is generated draft, not a published literary excerpt.

lessons.transfer_prompt: Add an original final sentence that supports one interpretation while leaving another possible. Explain your choice with the AI teacher.
lessons.sound_note: Compare живёт and здесь in natural speech. The scene’s punctuation helps track voices, but does not supply a recorded intonation model.
lessons.conversation_invitation: If you discuss a story together, share one possible interpretation and hear your friend’s. It can remain a conversation about the story.

targets.title: Greet and close
targets.description: Choose a greeting for the relationship and situation.

targets.title: Notice word stress
targets.description: Locate the prominent syllable without treating spelling as an audio test.

targets.title: Ask for conversational repair
targets.description: Request exactly the support needed.

targets.title: Make a polite request
targets.description: Use a useful -те request as a complete chunk.

targets.title: Connect Cyrillic to words
targets.description: Distinguish familiar-looking Cyrillic letters from Latin letters.

targets.title: Name an object
targets.description: Use Что это? / Это … to identify something.

targets.title: Introduce yourself
targets.description: Use Меня зовут … without assigning the learner a gender.

targets.title: Recognize я / вы / мы
targets.description: Connect person words to verb forms in useful chunks.

targets.title: Describe a location
targets.description: Use в / на with a learned locative phrase.

targets.title: Distinguish here and there
targets.description: Follow an actual pointing context.

targets.title: Use a direct object
targets.description: Recognize книгу and воду as objects in these sentences.

targets.title: Express a want
targets.description: Use Я хочу … and a polite service request appropriately.

targets.title: Describe possession
targets.description: Use у меня есть in a meaningful exchange.

targets.title: Describe absence
targets.description: Contrast есть книга with нет книги.

targets.title: Match a description to a noun
targets.description: Notice новый / новая / новое in naming phrases.

targets.title: Ask which one
targets.description: Use a description to identify the intended object.

targets.title: Identify actor and patient
targets.description: Use nominative / accusative names, rather than always choosing the first noun.

targets.title: Read meaning across word order
targets.description: Preserve roles when the patient is mentioned first.

targets.title: Locate an action in time
targets.description: Contrast сейчас / вчера / завтра with useful verb forms.

targets.title: Notice process and completion
targets.description: Compare reading activity with having read the whole book, without reducing aspect to tense.

targets.title: Name a destination
targets.description: Contrast в школу / в школе for going-to versus being-in.

targets.title: Describe directed movement
targets.description: Use иду for a current directed trip on foot, without treating it as every kind of going.

targets.title: Say can / cannot
targets.description: Use могу + infinitive for a concrete action.

targets.title: Propose a next action
targets.description: Use давайте and завтра in a short plan.

targets.title: Read an original speculative scene
targets.description: Integrate familiar language with a few glossed new words.

targets.title: Distinguish evidence and inference
targets.description: Say what is observed and what is not yet known.

targets.title: Read if … then
targets.description: Identify antecedent and consequence without confusing implication with its converse.

targets.title: Read existence and universality
targets.description: Distinguish существует from для каждого in a supported formal sentence.

targets.title: Give and request reasons
targets.description: Distinguish a conclusion from the reason offered for it.

targets.title: Express uncertainty
targets.description: Use думаю and не знаю without pretending certainty.

targets.title: Track a narrator and quoted speaker
targets.description: Attribute a claim to the right voice.

targets.title: Separate text and interpretation
targets.description: Explain a reading with an explicit reason from the text.

targets.title: Hear a hard/soft contrast
targets.description: Distinguish лук / люк from a real voice, separately from reading the spelling.

targets.title: Hear meaning-changing stress
targets.description: Distinguish за́мок / замо́к with audio and use stress marks only as a separate written scaffold.

phrases.translation: What is your name? (polite or plural)

phrases.note: Confirm preferred spelling, pronunciation, and stress of the learner’s name; Эмбер is a proposal.

phrases.note: Alternative past forms are supplied for choice with the AI teacher; the app must not infer the learner’s gender.

phrases.note: Alternative past forms are supplied for choice with the AI teacher; the app must not infer the learner’s gender.

phrases.russian: Если n делится на два, то n — чётное число.
phrases.stressed: Е́сли n де́лится на два, то n — чётное число́.

phrases.note: Supported mathematical bridge. Written symbols stay visible; ask the AI teacher to explain the spoken notation when you want to say them aloud.

script.name: а
script.cue: Vowel; its quality depends on stress and context.

script.name: бэ
script.cue: Can represent a hard or soft consonant; voicing can change in context.

script.name: вэ
script.cue: A Cyrillic consonant, not Latin B.

script.name: гэ
script.cue: Consonant; some grammatical endings have special pronunciation.

script.name: дэ
script.cue: Hard and soft counterparts occur; listen in a real word.

script.name: е
script.cue: After many consonants it helps mark softness; initially it can include a y-like onset.

script.name: ё
script.cue: Keep the dots. In the examples here ё carries stress; exceptions exist in Russian compounds and loans.

script.name: жэ
script.cue: Usually a hard consonant in standard Russian; not English j.

script.name: зэ
script.cue: Consonant with hard/soft counterparts; compare in natural speech.

script.name: и
script.cue: Vowel; often follows a soft consonant, but spelling after ж/ш is a separate pattern.

script.name: и кра́ткое
script.cue: A consonant, not another full vowel syllable.

script.name: ка
script.cue: Do not borrow Latin letter names when reading a word.

script.name: эль
script.cue: Hard and soft л can differ substantially.

script.name: эм
script.cue: Has hard and soft counterparts.

script.name: эн
script.cue: Cyrillic Н resembles Latin H but represents a different consonant.

script.name: о
script.cue: An unstressed о often differs from its stressed sound; listen to whole words.

script.name: пэ
script.cue: A consonant; softness and context matter.

script.name: эр
script.cue: Cyrillic Р is not Latin P; learn its sound from an AI speech model.

script.name: эс
script.cue: Cyrillic С is not English c in “cat”.

script.name: тэ
script.cue: The printed form is only one shape; cursive forms differ.

script.name: у
script.cue: A vowel; Cyrillic У is not Latin Y.

script.name: эф
script.cue: A consonant; practice in a familiar word.

script.name: ха
script.cue: A fricative; do not assume the English sound of letter x.

script.name: цэ
script.cue: An affricate, usually hard in standard pronunciation.

script.name: че
script.cue: Usually soft; что has a special standard pronunciation.

script.name: ша
script.cue: Usually hard in standard Russian.

script.name: ща
script.cue: A long soft fricative in common standard pronunciation; compare a real model.

script.name: твёрдый знак
script.cue: A separating sign, not an independent sound; advanced reference example follows.

script.name: ы
script.cue: A vowel distinct from и; a written distinction alone does not establish hearing it.

script.name: мя́гкий знак
script.cue: No independent vowel sound; can mark softness or serve other spelling functions.

script.name: э
script.cue: A vowel; compare это with familiar words containing е.

script.name: ю
script.cue: Initially can include a y-like onset; after many consonants helps mark softness.

script.name: я
script.cue: Initially can include a y-like onset; after many consonants helps mark softness.
